correctness.rationale: Every proper edge-subset of a simple cycle forms a forest, whose transposition product has one permutation cycle on each connected component. Distinct proper subsets can collide only if they are different spanning trees, and the full-edge word can collide only with a two-component forest word. Both cases reduce to the conjugacy equation t_j U=U t_i; path connectivity forces i,j to be earliest/latest in time and endpoint transport is equivalent to two increasing chronological arcs. Exactly two double fibres follow, and the binomial interleaving count gives \(k2^{k-2}\) bad orders. Entropy formulas are exact from fibre probabilities. Exhaustive finite cycle tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons establish that the recent Monte-shuffle result addresses many-step conditional mixing while the older tree-transposition works address full-support products or edge-order multiplicities on trees. The proposed exact two-double-fibre law and random-order \(1/(k-1)!\) bit loss are not direct consequences of these results. Actual Published-finding index synonym, equivalent-form and mechanism searches found related but non-dominating statements. Historical priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The simple cycle is the first natural departure from forests in a one-pass fair switching network. This complete classification identifies whether hidden switch bits can be reconstructed from the observed permutation, and quantifies the exact Shannon information deficit. The dichotomy between most lossless chronological orders and an exceptional factorially sparse family has direct interpretation for public schedule information and does not rely on unsupported mixing or security claims.
